samples.summary: New `--format csv` path on `ctx list`/`status` feeds server-controlled strings into a CSV writer with no formula-injection neutralization
samples.evidence: `parseOutputFormat` (formatter.ts:36) now legitimizes `csv` for two commands that previously ignored `--format` entirely, so `wafflebase ctx list --format csv` renders `name` — a string supplied by the server at login (login.ts:103, `GET /workspaces`) and renamable by any collaborator on a shared workspace — straight through `csvEscape` (csv.ts:15-24). `csvEscape` only quotes on `,`, `"` and `\n`; it does not prefix the leading `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, TAB or CR that Excel/LibreOffice interpret as a formula. Attack: a collaborator renames a shared workspace to `=cmd|'/c calc'!A1`; the victim runs `wafflebase ctx list --format csv > ws.csv` and opens it, executing the payload (DDE/formula injection). `status --format csv` has the same exposure for `user`, `email`, `server`, `workspaceName`. The helper itself is pre-existing and is arguably intentional for `sheets export` (spreadsheet content), but this change is what routes identity/metadata strings into it. I could not confirm the backend permits arbitrary workspace names, hence medium confidence.
searchedFor: grep 'formula injection|csvEscape|sanitiz' across packages (only csv.ts, notes preview, frontend export-utils match)
read packages/cli/src/output/csv.ts in full — no leading =/+/-/@ handling

samples.summary: `--format` still unvalidated at the one `output()` call site that prints a one-time secret; the new `format()` throw destroys the freshly created key after the server-side mutation
samples.evidence: The change adds `parseOutputFormat` and a throwing `default:` branch in `format()` (formatter.ts:51-56) but applies the validator only to `status`, `ctx list` and `schema`. `api-keys create` still calls `output(res.data, opts.format, false)` with the raw flag, and does so *after* `createApiKey(name)` has already succeeded. With `--format bogus` the new `default:` throws inside the existing try, `outputError` prints INVALID_FORMAT, and the raw key — which the comment on line 19 says is shown only once — is never displayed, leaving a live credential on the server that the operator never saw. Validation belongs before the mutating request. Pre-existing in effect (the old code printed a literal `undefined` and lost the key the same way), so this is a missed hardening rather than a regression; recoverable via `api-keys list`/`revoke`, hence minor.
searchedFor: grep 'output\(|outputError\(|opts\.format|parseOutputFormat' across packages/cli/src — enumerated all 31 output() call sites
read packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts to confirm format() now throws rather than returning undefined

samples.summary: `status`/`ctx list` widen default-on stdout from truncated prose to full identifiers (full workspace UUIDs, email, exact token expiry) in machine-readable form
samples.evidence: The removed code deliberately truncated identifiers: status printed `${ws.name} (${activeWorkspace.slice(0, 8)}...)` and `formatWorkspaceList` printed `ws.id.slice(0, 8)`. `buildStatus` (status.ts:50) and `buildWorkspaceList` (ctx.ts:28) now emit full UUIDs, plus `email` and `expiresAt`, as JSON by default — and both docs pages now tell agents to run these as the standard probe. Agent transcripts and CI logs routinely capture stdout, so the blast radius of a leaked log grows from an 8-char prefix to full workspace identifiers and PII. No token material is emitted (verified: `accessToken`/`refreshToken` are not referenced by `buildStatus`), so this is exposure surface, not credential leakage.

samples.summary: `loggedIn: true` / `session: 'valid'` are now a machine contract derived from a locally stored, signature-unverified JWT claim and never checked against the server
samples.evidence: `buildStatus` derives `session: 'valid'` from `isSessionExpired` (session.ts:85), which compares `session.expiresAt` — a value written at login by `decodeJwtExpiry` (session.ts:96-113), which base64-decodes the JWT payload without verifying the signature and never re-validates. The change promotes this to a documented, agent-facing field (registry.ts response shape; cli.md "agents branch on `loggedIn`"), so an agent will treat a server-side-revoked or remotely-logged-out session as authenticated, and anyone who can write `~/.wafflebase/session.json` or set `WAFFLEBASE_SESSION` can make `status` assert a valid session with forged `user`/`email`. That writer already holds the tokens, so this is a trust-boundary/labelling weakness rather than an escalation — hence low confidence on real-world impact.
